To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

preschoolers' cognitive transformations of the delay-relevant qualities of a superhero (e.g., patient vs. impatient) can be induced by a superhero's qualities (e.g., Superman's patient vs. impatienet qualities) and that the delay-relevant cognitive transformation of Superman (e.g., being patient like Superman) can be induced through the superhero's qualities and the superhero's behavior (e.g., watching a video of a patient Superman).

preschoolers can be induced to delay gratification longer when they are instructed to imagine themselves as superheroes, and when they are instructed regarding the superhero's delay-relevant characteristics.

Caped preschoolers delay gratification longer, especially when the caped superhero's relevant qualities are emphasized, and especially when the child is instructed to pretend to have the same qualities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
cognitive self-transformation as a process in which children's cognitive self-concepts and self-definitions play a role.
cognitive self-transformation as a cognitive process that is involved in the delay of immediate gratification.
the cognitive self-transformation of preschoolers in the delay of-gratification paradigm.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

cognitive self-transformation is the process by which the child, by means of a cognitive process, transforms his or her own self into another self, in the sense of a self that has a different cognitive structure.
cognitive self-transformation can lead to longer delays in the delay of reward paradigm.
children's delay behavior is affected by their cognitive self-transformation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cognitive transformations are basic processes that are not limited to the reward's consumulatory value, but can be used in other cognitive processes.
cognitive self-transformation can be achieved through a variety of cognitive means and that the cognitive transformation is not a simple function of the cognitive means used.
cognitive self-transformation can occur in the context of a delay of gratification task, but it is not the only factor affecting children's delay of gratification.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cognitive self-transformation can be a powerful tool for increasing children's self-control, even in the preschool years.
cognitive self-transformation may be a key factor in the development of self-control. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2019 APA, all rights reserved)
